summary: Required arm and foot anatomy is within the close-up frames, so cropping does not invalidate the capture. However, rear claws are partly occluded, the full-body three-quarter view is obstructed, and substantial visual mismatches remain. The technical report also records two arm/torso penetration blockers.

findings.message: The supplied technical report records 0.87-stud torso penetration for each upper arm, exceeding the 0.70-stud limit. Visually, both shoulder attachments merge heavily into the chest; screenshots cannot independently verify the measurements.
findings.recommendation: Move both upper arms outward and rerun the penetration check.

findings.message: The supplied report gives a height/depth ratio of 1.16 against a 1.25 threshold. The static pose nevertheless reads as an upright biped.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the measured silhouette ratio with the intended torso posture and counterbalance tail.

findings.message: The muzzle faces forward, but stacked rectangular muzzle/jaw blocks and rounded cheek masses do not establish the target's predator face. Low yellow eyes and a deep, anatomically distinct lower jaw are not readable. Rounded stone-like body masses lack the target's integrated hide and fissures.
findings.recommendation: Reshape the muzzle, brows, cheeks, and lower jaw into coherent animal anatomy; establish visible yellow eyes and restrained fissures.

findings.message: Both hands have straight wedge claws rather than downward-curving animal claws. All three front claws on each foot are visible, but they read as flat blades. Rear-claw glimpses in the foot and side views do not establish one unobscured rear claw per foot. This is occlusion, not cropping.
findings.recommendation: Shape curved claws and distinct paw digits, strengthen the elevated hocks, and expose each rear claw in dedicated views.

findings.message: The dorsal elements read as narrow angular spikes rather than broad volcanic slabs. Five distinct primary assemblies, their root clearance, and the rise toward plates 3 and 4 cannot be verified. Four tail plates are readable from the sides, but appear separated above the tail rather than clearly rooted into it.
findings.recommendation: Build five separated slab assemblies with exposed roots and the specified height rhythm; seat four tail plates visibly along the tail arc.

findings.message: A foreground object obscures much of the full-body three-quarter view. Red, white-outlined arm overlays also obscure upper-arm surfaces and prevent reliable assessment of their underlying appearance.
findings.recommendation: Isolate the model and disable diagnostic overlays before recapturing.

criteria.reason: Bipedal stance, dark coloration, and a dorsal tail rhythm provide broad resemblance, but the target's predator anatomy, volcanic slabs, and yellow fissures are not established.
The captured stance is upright with an exposed broad chest and unsupported arms. Static views cannot verify that the arms never support the body or that posture remains upright in motion.
Broad torso and thick limb masses are present, but exposed narrow connectors, rounded segmented anatomy, and weak hock definition undermine powerful continuous proportions.
Forward orientation is correct, but the rectangular muzzle, indistinct lower jaw, and unreadable yellow eyes fail the required bestial predator treatment.
Neither hand clearly establishes three primary digits plus a short side digit; visible claws are straight wedges rather than downward curves.
Each foot has three visible forward claws. Neither foot close-up establishes all rear-claw anatomy unobscured, and high rear hocks are insufficiently distinct.
Side and rear views show a heavy tail made of overlapping tapered cylinder segments, with its tip above the ground.
Four tail plates are readable, but five separated primary volcanic slab assemblies, exposed roots, and the required height rhythm are not verifiable; the visible shapes read as spikes.
A small sternum accent and limited armor are present, but organic hide, yellow eyes, and faint yellow fissures are not clearly established. Arm overlays obscure additional surface evidence.
The simplified head and spike-backed silhouette do not establish a distinct original predator identity. Diagnostic overlays also prevent verification of the underlying arm coloration.
